Subject: Post-demo recap & immediate next steps (model fit, evals, JSON-schema tests)

Hi Ariel — thanks again for a great session today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Optio Health wants poster-quality extraction of encounter summaries and structured meds/allergies for downstream analytics.
- Primary concerns: hallucination on numeric fields (dosage), schema-compliance for downstream ingestion, and predictable 95th%-tile latency under 300ms.

Redwood recommendations (starter pack):
1) Model tiers to try (we can spin up test endpoints):
   - Redwood-Instruct-3B-Quant: best latency/cost balance for high-throughput batch evals.
   - Redwood-Align-7B: higher-context fidelity for complex discharge summaries (slower but better quality).
   - Fallback: Redwood-Chat-1.3B for low-cost prototyping and A/B baseline.

2) Evals and artifacts I attached: optio_eval_benchmarks_20260213.pdf (benchmarks vs your sample), prompt_suite_v1.csv (recommended prompt sets and temperature sweeps), json_schema_examples.json (expected output schemas for tool-calling/structured responses).

3) Tool/function calling & schema enforcement:
   - We recommend exercising "function call" mode with strict JSON schema validation (schema in attached json_schema_examples.json).
   - For retries: use deterministic idempotency keys on your ingestion side, and have Redwood’s runtime return a validation flag in the response header so you can retry only on legitimate transient failures.

Immediate asks for Optio team to unblock a short POC (2–4 weeks):
- Share a representative sample of 300 records we can use for the JSON-schema compliance run (CSV/NDJSON).
- Confirm target P95 latency you want to validate and any hard cost constraints.
- Agree on one model variant to start (I recommend Redwood-Instruct-3B-Quant for the first run).

Next steps I propose this week:
- Dev will send a short runbook + sample cURL to call the schema-enforced endpoint (see his note below).
- We’ll schedule a 30-min tech sync to go through your sample and one example prompt set — can you do Mon 16th or Tue 17th?

Thanks — Rishi

Hi Ariel — quick technical notes and a sample cURL to exercise schema-enforced tool-calling. TL;DR: runtime can validate and return structured error objects; we also provide a "validation_passed" boolean in the response metadata if you use the function-calling endpoint.

Behavioral summary:
- If response fails JSON schema validation: endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body:
  {
    "validation_passed": false,
    "errors": ["/medications[2].dose: expected number, got "50mg""],
    "raw_output": "..."
  }

- We also support a strict mode (HTTP 400) if you prefer to treat schema failures as request errors.

Retries and idempotency:
- Include an idempotency key on each request (X-Idempotency-Key). If an ingestion write fails downstream, signal back with a 202 + validation_passed=false and don’t write to the canonical store until ingestion ACKs. This avoids duplicate downstream writes.

Sample cURL (schema-enforced function call):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/funcalls/run \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: optio-enc-20260213-001" \n  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-instruct-3b-quant",
    "prompt": "<prompt template id=encounter_summary_v1>",
    "function_schema": <contents of json_schema_examples.json>,
    "strict_schema_mode": true
  }'

Attached I put a small sample run we can execute on your 300-records once you share them. I can also kick off an internal eval run and upload CSV of model outputs to the Drive link Rishi included.

If useful, I’ll run a cost/latency matrix across the three model variants and send a short spreadsheet Monday.

Cheers,
Dev
